rules.text: The only call-site spelling is `§A{ref}`, `§A{out}` or `§A{in}` on a named-target call (`§C{target}`), optionally combined with a named argument as `§A{out}[name] operand`. The brace must touch the marker. Any other spelling, including a new declaration form, requires a versioned amendment of this contract and a migration decision.
Any other modifier text, and any modifier on an expression-target call, constructor (`§NEW`) or collection argument list, is refused with Calor0107. A modifier is never dropped silently.
Parameter declarations keep the existing `(T:name:ref|out|in)` form. The C# emitter writes the modifier on the same argument, and C# to Calor to C# round trips keep each argument's modifier and name.
Statement calls and expression calls, static and instance calls, follow the same rules. An instance receiver is evaluated before the arguments.
Named and reordered arguments are evaluated in source order. The emitted call keeps source order and C# argument names; it is never reordered into parameter order.

Modifiers take part in overload selection. The call-site modifier must equal the selected parameter's kind (ref with ref, out with out, in with in). A missing or different modifier is refused (Calor0208 today); it must never select a by-value overload.

The return value of a by-reference call can be used wherever an expression can. The callee's writes are visible to every read that C# evaluates after the call, including later operands of the same expression.

A ref or out operand is accepted exactly where a direct `§ASSIGN` to the same operand is accepted, and C# also accepts it as a variable: a mutable or immutable local binding, a by-value, ref or out parameter, an instance or static field that is not readonly (bare, `this.`, qualified or through a reference-type receiver), an array element of any rank, and a field path of value-type fields rooted at one of these. Parity with `§ASSIGN` also covers immutable bindings and loop variables, which `§ASSIGN` accepts at the measured commit; if the language later rejects those assignments, by-reference operands follow.

Calor refuses, before C# generation, every operand C# cannot pass by reference: a literal, a computed expression, a call result, a property, an indexer (any `§IDX` whose receiver is not an array), a readonly field outside a constructor, an `in` parameter, and `this`. The refusal is a Calor semantic diagnostic (symbol InvalidByReferenceOperand, allocated by #943); a generated-C# failure (Calor1002) does not count as a refusal.

`§A{in}` takes the same operands as `ref`, plus `in` parameters and readonly fields. An `in` parameter needs `§A{in}` at the call site; a call without it is refused (Calor0208 today). C# calls that pass an rvalue to an `in` parameter, or omit `in`, are preserved or refused, not converted natively.

A by-reference argument denotes the caller's storage. The generated C# passes that same storage location. No temporary, hoist or copy of the operand, or of any value-type step of its path, is allowed (F1-REFOUT-08).

A receiver may be hoisted into a local only when its static type is a reference type (class, interface, array, delegate, string) and the hoist evaluates it exactly once, in the original order. A value type, Nullable<T>, a type parameter not constrained to `class`, or an unknown type is never hoisted.
Copy-in/copy-out emulation (pass a temporary, write it back after the call) is forbidden. It differs from C# under aliasing and exceptions.
When no native operand form exists, the converter preserves the enclosing member or statement as C# interop, or refuses. Such cases count as preserved or rejected in every report, never as native.

The same storage passed in two by-reference positions is one location; the callee's write order decides the result. Storage the callee can also reach directly (a static field) aliases the by-reference parameter.
A by-value argument that names the same storage is read at its own argument position, before the call.

Receiver first, then arguments left to right in source order. For an element operand, the array reference and indices are evaluated, and null, bounds and array-covariance checks happen, at the operand's position: before later arguments and before the callee runs.
A by-reference call in a conditional position stays conditional and is evaluated as often as in C#. It is never hoisted out of `&&`, `||`, `?:`, `??`, or a loop condition.
A ref operand must be initialized before the call. An out operand need not be. After normal completion the out operand holds the callee's value.

Writes the callee makes before throwing stay in the caller's storage, for both ref and out. After an exceptional exit the caller may assume neither the old value nor that the out operand was assigned.

Native Calor gets no inline out declaration. The converter lowers C# `out var x` or `out T x` to a mutable binding of the declared type, placed immediately before the innermost enclosing statement in the same block (never outside a loop body or other scope), and passes `§A{out} x`. It does so only when the type is known and expressible, the name collides with no other name in the callable (including converter-generated names), and the declaration is not in a field or property initializer, constructor initializer, query, `when` filter, or expression-bodied lambda. Otherwise it preserves the statement or member as C#. FeatureSupport's `out-var` entry must match this rule.

`§A{out} _` is always a discard and emits `out _`, in module functions and class methods alike. When C# `_` binds to a declared variable rather than a discard, the converter must not emit a discard. `§A{ref} _` and `§A{in} _` are refused.
By-reference operands keep their native types. No Option, Result, tuple, multi-return, StrongBox or wrapper-class representation is introduced, and no out parameter is turned into a return value.

This contract consumes docs/plans/v0.22-nullability-enforcement-scoping.md at d0dc0f8bf3ea400b1d7d16780a98d9ff3341abc7: `?str` is a nullable reference, not Option<T>; new ref/out syntax and flow-dependent interop attributes are outside 0.22. By-reference transfers are not 0.22 receiving boundaries, and this contract activates no Calor0272/0273/0274 diagnostic for them.
After a ref or out call, every flow narrowing of the operand is invalidated. The operand has its declared type. No fact is derived from the call's return value.

Flow-dependent attributes (NotNullWhen, MaybeNullWhen, NotNullIfNotNull, MaybeNull, NotNull, AllowNull, DisallowNull, MemberNotNull, MemberNotNullWhen, DoesNotReturn, DoesNotReturnIf) are inert metadata and are never interpreted. Code that type-checks only through such an attribute is preserved or refused, not converted natively. The converter never inserts `!`, defaults or throws.

A by-reference parameter typed by a type parameter of a generic type, substituted from the receiver (Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.TryGetValue), may be called natively; the operand's state after the call is Oblivious (unknown), never non-null. A by-reference parameter typed by a method type parameter (TryCast<T>(object, out T)) is preserved or refused (F1-REFOUT-07).

For natively declared parameters, a ref or out operand's declared type must equal the parameter type, including the scalar nullable annotation. A mismatch in either direction is refused (Calor0208 at the measured commit).

A ref or out argument charges the caller the effect that a direct `§ASSIGN` to the same operand charges: `mut` for an array element, a field through a receiver, or a dotted path; nothing for a local or parameter. `in` charges no write. Sub-expressions of the operand charge their read effects.
Assigning a by-reference parameter inside the callee charges nothing extra there; RO-EFF-1 charges the caller, who chose the storage.

The write charge depends on the call-site modifier and operand, not on callee resolution. An unresolved or BCL callee keeps the existing unknown-call handling (Calor0410 or Calor0419) and is never treated as pure because it takes by-reference arguments.

A bare-name field operand (`§A{ref} n`) charges what `§ASSIGN n` charges at the measured commit, which is nothing. Changing bare-field charging is outside this contract and must change both forms together.

Consistent with R-OBL (#1496, ba2e31cb): a name passed as ref or out anywhere in a body is a written name. Every entry or guard fact that reads it is stale for the whole body. A fact that reads an element, field or dotted path is stale once the body contains any call. This holds for unresolved callees.

An `in` argument does not make its operand a written name. Aliasing does: when a callable has two or more by-reference parameters and writes one, or has a by-reference parameter and may change the heap, all of them are written names.

An obligation that reads a stale name is never reported as a failed proof (Calor1121/Calor1140) from that state. It is Calor1124 (unsupported) with its runtime check kept, or discharged from facts that are not stale. Guards are elided only for discharged obligations.
The verification cache must distinguish modifiers: a result cached for `§A x` is never reused for `§A{ref} x` or `§A{out} x`.

Bug-pattern checks (division by zero, null dereference, index bounds, overflow) must not use the pre-call value or range of a ref or out operand after the call. If a check cannot model the call, it reports nothing as safe because of it.
A body containing preserved C# (`§CS`, `§CSHARP`, raw blocks) has no facts (R-OBL opacity). By-reference calls inside preserved C# are covered by that rule, not modelled.

Outside this slice, preserved as counted C# interop or refused, never native: ref locals and ref returns, ref readonly parameters and returns, `scoped`, ref structs and their indexers (Span<T>), ref fields, `this ref` extension methods, by-reference arguments to constructors and constructor initializers, delegates and function pointers with by-reference parameters, by-reference arguments through `dynamic`, pointers and unsafe code, and method-generic by-reference parameters.

Preserved shapes are counted and reported as interop. FeatureSupport's `out-var` (claims Full) and `ref-parameter`/`out-parameter` (recommend tuples) entries must be corrected by #943 to describe this contract.
Regression controls F1-REFOUT-01, 03, 05 and 06 stay native-match on all four R0 surfaces. Calls without modifiers are unchanged.

diagnostics.meaning: A ref, out or in operand that C# cannot pass by reference (RO-LV-2, RO-DECL-2). Reported by the binder before C# generation.

cases.note: Refused only by the generated C# compile (Calor1002) at the measured commit.
Parity: `§ASSIGN v 2` on the same immutable binding is accepted at the measured commit (D1-LV-07).
Parity control for D1-LV-06.
Parity: `§ASSIGN i 5` inside the same loop is accepted at the measured commit.
The same element operand is accepted in a class method (D1-LV-10) but refused with Calor0208 in a module function.
`§ASSIGN k.n 3` in the same position binds and charges `mut`; the by-reference form is refused with Calor0208.
In a module function `_` is reported as an undefined variable (Calor0200).
Refused today only because `_` is undefined; the refusal must name the discard.
Control D1-NULL-06 shows the same narrowing is accepted without the call.
A heap write through `ref` is not charged `mut`; the direct assignment (D1-EFF-03) is.
Parity control for D1-EFF-01 and D1-EFF-02.
Parity control for D1-LV-09: a bare-name field write charges nothing at the measured commit.
An unresolved callee keeps the unknown-call charge (Calor0410 with warning Calor0411); by-reference arguments do not make it pure.
A resolved pure BCL callee writing a local charges nothing.
SetNeg writes -5: a discharge from the stale precondition would be a false proof.
`Two(ref v, ref v)` makes `a` zero.
#943 adds the cache witness: the same body with `§A y` (by value) proved first, then this body, must not reuse the result.

cases.witness: §B{~d:i32} 1, then a callee that assigns its ref parameter 0, then (/ 10 d). At the measured commit the division-by-zero check reports nothing with or without the call, so no executable witness discriminates yet. #943 must add one (or a different checker that uses constant values) before READY.

A body whose by-reference call is kept as inline `§CS{}` (F1-REFOUT-02's `out var` before repair) has no facts: a `§Q` fact on the out operand does not discharge a later `§PROOF`. Covered by R-OBL's opacity rule; #943 adds the witness.
